metadata.file_name: 116. Ye & Yuan. (2022). Using a machine learning approach to explore non-cognitive factors affecting reading, mathematics, and science literacy in china and the united states.pdf
metadata.title: USING A MACHINE LEARNING APPROACH TO EXPLORE NON-COGNITIVE FACTORS AFFECTING READING, MATHEMATICS, AND SCIENCE LITERACY IN CHINA AND THE UNITED STATES

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses OECD PISA 2018 microdata for 15-year-olds from China (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang) and the United States, with dependent variables derived from PISA achievement scores (PV1READ, PV1MATH, PV1SCIE) and independent variables drawn from student, family, and school questionnaires. The manuscript reports stratified sampling in PISA and describes sample filtering via deletion of invalid questionnaires and removal of cases with more than half missing values, but it does not report applying PISA complex survey weights or replicate weights in the CART training. Because the analysis is a machine-learning decision-tree approach and the paper does not mention weight-aware estimation tools, weighting is treated as not reported/unclear. The authors also preprocess missing values by setting missing entries to 0, deleting cases with >50% missingness, and then imputing remaining missing values using k-nearest neighbors interpolation before fitting CART.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 education dataset for 15-year-old students from China’s four provinces/cities (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang) and the United States. After deleting invalid questionnaires, the final analytic sample was 11,977 students in China and 4,838 in the United States. For preprocessing, the authors set missing values of variables to 0, deleted samples with more than half of the missing value, and then applied k-nearest neighbor interpolation for remaining missingness; they then constructed low vs high ability groups using achievement level thresholds (reading levels 2 and below vs 3+; mathematics levels 3 and below vs 4+; science levels 3 and below vs 4+).

main_findings.target_variable: Reading achievement (low vs high using PV1READ thresholds)
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading data (PV1READ; 15-year-olds), the study leveraged meta-cognition credibility (METASPAM), text summarizing (METASUM), understanding/remembering (UNDREM), perceived test difficulty (PISADIFF), and ESCS to classify students into low vs high reading ability, finding that self-awareness/metacognitive variables were among the most influential predictors and that ESCS was a key family-level factor in China. This indicates that strengthening students’ metacognitive study practices and targeting low-ESCS students with additional learning support may improve reading outcomes, though the CART results are predictive and do not establish causal effects.

main_findings.target_variable: Mathematics achievement (low vs high using PV1MATH thresholds)
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Mathematics data (PV1MATH; 15-year-olds), the study leveraged METASPAM, METASUM, PISADIFF, and school learning-time indicators (SMINS and ST060Q01NA) to classify students into low vs high mathematics ability, finding that metacognitive awareness and school learning opportunities were prominent across China and that cooperation/competition-related factors also mattered for mathematics and science. This indicates that policies promoting structured learning time and classroom practices that balance cooperative and competitive engagement may support mathematics achievement, while the study’s preprocessing and lack of reported model metrics/weights limit precision and generalizability.

main_findings.target_variable: Science achievement (low vs high using PV1SCIE thresholds)
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Science data (PV1SCIE; 15-year-olds), the study leveraged PISADIFF, METASPAM, METASUM, and school learning-time indicators (SMINS and ST060Q01NA) to classify students into low vs high science ability, finding that student-level self-awareness/metacognition and school instructional time were key common predictors and that cooperation/competition dynamics supported science performance. This indicates that science improvement strategies should combine metacognitive skill development with adequate, well-organized instructional time, while the CART approach remains correlational/predictive rather than causal.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes OECD PISA 2018 microdata for 15-year-olds in China (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang; N=11,977) and the United States (N=4,838). It uses CART decision trees to classify students into low vs high achievement groups using PV1READ, PV1MATH, and PV1SCIE thresholds (reading: level ≤2 vs ≥3; math/science: level ≤3 vs ≥4). Missing values were handled by setting missing entries to 0, deleting cases with more than half missingness, and applying k-nearest-neighbor interpolation; the paper does not report applying PISA sampling/replicate weights. Across both countries, metacognition-related indices (METASPAM, METASUM) and perceived test difficulty (PISADIFF) repeatedly appear among the most influential predictors, while ESCS/WEALTH and school learning-time variables (SMINS, ST060Q01NA) differ in importance by country. Model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC) are not reported, so the practical magnitude of effects and robustness cannot be fully assessed; results should be interpreted as predictive associations rather than causal impacts.
